_comment: Single configuration file for the AIMOTOR CANopen library. Edit paths / adapters / motors here - nothing is hardcoded in the Python sources.

paths._comment: base_dir null = folder of this library (derived from __file__). Put an absolute path here to move the library. Relative paths are resolved against base_dir.

adapters._comment: One entry per physical CAN adapter. Each motor names the adapter its bus is on. 'serial' pins a profile to one physical CANable2 - gs_usb index order is NOT stable across replug. Read serials with Examples/example_00_list_adapters.py.

canable2_left.notes: LEFT motor bus, node 1. Separate physical adapter and separate CAN bus. 250000 bps crashes libusb on this PC - do not use.

canable2_right.notes: RIGHT motor bus, node 2. Separate physical adapter and separate CAN bus.

canable2.notes: Single-bus fallback. Same device as canable2_left when only one adapter is plugged in.

canalystii.notes: Alternative adapter. Motor is wired to CAN1, which is channel 0.

socketcan.notes: For a future Linux / ROS2 host.

virtual.notes: Offline dry run, no hardware needed.

shutdown.notes: MUST stay false with more than one motor: exiting during teardown would leave the other motor armed. Motor_Group forces it false and disarms every motor before any bus is closed.

limits._comment: Drive nameplate: rated 3000 rpm, hard max 3600 rpm (H00_15). No 0x6072/0x6080 object exists, so these limits are enforced in software before every write.

profile._comment: Units are Pul/s and Pul/s^2. At 1000 pulses/rev: 16667 pul/s = 1000 rpm, 50000 pul/s = 3000 rpm.

Left.description: AIMOTOR servo, node 1 (H0C_00=1), 1 Mbps (H0C_08=6), on its own CANable2.

Right.description: AIMOTOR servo, node 2 (H0C_00=2), 1 Mbps (H0C_08=6), on its own CANable2.

pairing._comment: Used by the paired drive controls in the GUI and by example_06. invert_right_for_forward true suits a differential base, where the right wheel faces the other way, so a positive forward command drives straight.
